chapter: Cab Calloway on the road and segregation
title: The Memphis ballroom riot over Cab's autograph
summary: A white woman asking Cab's autograph set off a huge fight with the band chased to the train.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What about Jim Crow in those days, with the Cab Calloway band. Now the band was very popular, it appeared in movies and, obviously, it was a band that attracted a lot of white people also, or was known among white people.
And when you were touring, what -- were there incidents, was it --

Oh, were there incidents. We were in Memphis, Tennessee, and at the end of the dance, there was a white girl came up -- woman -- for Cab's autograph. And you know how Cab, reach over the stand, his hair would fall right on down. And the biggest fight started you ever saw in
Because this woman came up and his hair fell down like that. I don't know why that -- I mean the fight started then.

Chairs, bottles, everything, the biggest fight you ever saw in your life in the ballroom. Free-for-all, throwing at the band, fighting the band. Chairs, I got behind a table. I just got behind a table. I can't fight. Then a pig got his knife out and it was a good fight. Cops came and hustled Cab out, took him out the back and put him in a car, and we didn't see Cab anymore until we got on the train. But they were fighting us all the way out of the ballroom, all the way from the -- in the automobiles, on the highways, till we got all the way to the train. Throwing bricks at the cars, everything, all the way till we got to the Pullman car. Cab was in the Pullman car, sleeping.
When was this, do you remember?
Actually, the year, I can't remember that, it in the '30's, the dates, I don't remember. I don't remember the date of that.
And there were many incidents similar?
